title: fork_nested_in_branch
description: Finding 1 (PR #34): a fork branch that itself contains a nested fork must carry the branch's iteration ordinal as a recombination key, mirroring the CHAIN path. Without it the nested fork recombines on the parent key alone and cross-joins across the branch's iterations. Two cases: (1) a typed forEach fork branch with a nested forEach fork; (2) the JSON-bridge hole (`:539`) - a forEach over a repeat-forced field, sibling of the repeat, that itself contains a nested fork. Distinct values throughout so the order-independent Set comparison cannot mask a spurious cross-join row.

tests.title: nested fork inside a typed forEach fork branch recombines per iteration
tests.description: Root forks on forEach:contact (nested fork forEach:name + forEach:telecom) and a sibling forEach:identifier, over a Patient with two contacts. name/telecom must recombine per contact, not cross-join across contacts.

tests.title: nested fork inside a JSON-bridge forEach fork branch recombines per iteration
tests.description: A repeat over `item` forces `item` to JSON[]; a sibling forEach:item (jsonMode, the `:539` hole) itself forks on forEach:answer + forEach:item. Over two top-level items the nested answer/child-item fork must recombine per top item, not cross-join across items.
